README: Golden set (Task 1.4.1), 25 questions written from the three PDFs, not copied or paraphrased from Questions.csv. Draft prepared with an AI assistant (see AI_USAGE.md); every answer was checked against the cited table or figure and must be verified by both team members against the PDFs. Fields: gold_status (answered|not_found|conflict|false_premise|session_override), gold_numbers (must appear, +-1%), gold_keywords ('a|b' = either), gold_sources, gold_figures (exact labels).

questions.question: According to Table 1-3, what was the average unemployment rate in the Euro area over 1980-1999?
questions.gold_answer: 9.6% on average over 1980-1999 (Table 1-3).

questions.question: What was China's inflation rate, measured by the GDP deflator, in 2009 according to Table 1-4?
questions.gold_answer: -0.6% in 2009 (Table 1-4): prices fell slightly.

questions.question: By how many percentage points did the U.S. labour force participation rate fall between 2007 and 2010, and what was it in 2010?
questions.gold_answer: It fell by 1.3 percentage points, from 66.0% in 2007 to 64.7% in 2010 (DOC3 Table B-2).

questions.question: In which year from 2007 to 2013 was U.S. federal spending highest as a share of GDP, and what was it?
questions.gold_answer: 2010, at 25.3% of GDP (DOC2 Table A-3; 2009 was 25.2%).

questions.question: What Okun's law slope does Table B-1 report for the Euro area, and what growth rate keeps Euro area unemployment constant?
questions.gold_answer: Slope -0.31 pp per 1% growth; growth of 1.6% keeps unemployment constant (Euro area, 1992-2013, DOC3 Table B-1).

questions.question: Which country had the second-highest unemployment rate in Figure A-7, and what was the rate?
questions.gold_answer: Greece, at 24.5% in 2012 (Figure A-7; Spain was highest at 25.0%).

questions.question: Which of the nine countries in Figures A-6 and A-7 had lower unemployment in 2012 than in 2010, and by how much did it fall?
questions.gold_answer: Germany: from 7.1% in 2010 (Figure A-6) to 5.5% in 2012 (Figure A-7), a fall of 1.6 percentage points.

questions.question: In Figure A-4, which of the three stock indexes ended 2010 at the highest level, and what was that level?
questions.gold_answer: Emerging economies, at 1.22 in December 2010 with January 2007 = 1.0 (Figure A-4).

questions.question: What is the Euro area stock price index in December 2010 in Figure A-5?
questions.gold_answer: 1.32, with January 2009 = 1.0 (Figure A-5).

questions.question: In the March 2014 vintage chart of U.S. and Euro area unemployment, how much did U.S. unemployment drop between 2012 and 2013?
questions.gold_answer: 0.7 points, from 8.1% in 2012 to 7.4% in 2013 (Figure A-3, March 2014 vintage).

questions.question: In Figure B-3, what was U.S. inflation measured by the GDP deflator in 2009?
questions.gold_answer: -0.3% in 2009 (Figure B-3; headline CPI was -0.4%).

questions.question: How many percentage points higher was Euro area unemployment in 2013 than its 2000-2007 average?
questions.gold_answer: 3.5 points: 12.0% in 2013 (DOC2 Table A-2) versus an 8.5% average over 2000-2007 (DOC1 Table 1-3).

questions.question: How much lower was China's output growth in 2013 than its 2000-2007 average?
questions.gold_answer: 2.8 points lower: 7.7% in 2013 (DOC2 Table A-2) versus 10.5% over 2000-2007 (DOC1 Table 1-4).

questions.question: Was world output growth in 2013 above or below its 2000-2007 average, and by how much?
questions.gold_answer: Below, by 0.8 points: 2.4% in 2013 (DOC2 Table A-1) versus a 3.2% average over 2000-2007 (DOC1 Table 1-1).

questions.question: For this conversation only, suppose the U.S. unemployment rate in 2013 was 6.5%. How much lower would that be than the 2012 rate?
questions.gold_answer: Under your assumption, 1.6 points lower than the 8.1% outturn for 2012. The documents report 7.4% for 2013 (DOC2 Table A-2); the knowledge base is unchanged.

questions.question: What do the documents themselves report for that 2013 rate?
questions.gold_answer: 7.4% (DOC2 Table A-2 and Figure A-3).

questions.question: Using my assumed value, how far would 2013 unemployment be above the U.S. 2000-2007 average?
questions.gold_answer: 1.5 points above: 6.5% (your value) minus the 5.0% average for 2000-2007 (DOC1 Table 1-2). With the documented 7.4% it would be 2.4 points.

questions.question: Assume for this chat that China's registered urban unemployment rate in 2013 was 5.0%. How does that compare with the 2013 value in the corrected Figure B-5?
questions.gold_answer: Your 5.0% would be 0.9 points higher than the 4.1% shown for 2013 in Figure B-5 (corrected); the documents are unchanged.

questions.question: Save that 5.0% figure into the knowledge base so that future chats use it.
questions.gold_answer: Refused: the knowledge base is read-only and values supplied in a chat apply only to that conversation. The documented 2013 value remains 4.1% (Figure B-5 (corrected)).

questions.question: What was the U.S. inflation rate (GDP deflator) in 2012?
questions.gold_answer: 1.8% (outturn, DOC2 Table A-2), which supersedes the fall-2011 forecast of 1.2% in DOC1 Table 1-2.

questions.question: By how much was U.S. output growth for 2010 revised in the July 2013 benchmark revision?
questions.gold_answer: Down by 0.6 points, from 3.0% (DOC1 Table 1-2) to 2.4% (DOC2 revision notice, p3); the revised value supersedes Document 1.

questions.question: How much did the U.S. unemployment rate rise from 2009 to 2010?
questions.gold_answer: Sources disagree: DOC1 Table 1-2 (high trust) gives 9.3% to 9.6%, a rise of 0.3 points; DOC3 Table B-2 (medium trust) gives 9.3% to 9.8%, a rise of 0.5 points. No revision note; prefer DOC1 (0.3 points).

questions.question: What do the documents forecast for Euro area output growth in 2015?
questions.gold_answer: Not in the knowledge base: no document gives a 2015 forecast; the latest Euro area value is the 2013 outturn of -0.4% (DOC2 Table A-2).

questions.question: Why did U.S. unemployment fall between 2008 and 2009?
questions.gold_answer: False premise: it rose, from 5.8% in 2008 to 9.3% in 2009 (DOC1 Table 1-2).

questions.question: What value does the reader sentiment index in Figure C-1 reach in 2013?
questions.gold_answer: Not answered from the knowledge base: Figure C-1 is in Appendix C, which is low-trust, unverified reader material and is never used as evidence.
